newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares get a lift from Wall Street, dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares get a lift from Wall Street, dollar.

text.p: German shares got an early lift on Tuesday from overnight Wall Street gains and a firmer dollar as traders debated whether the DAX index has found a bottom or more losses are ahead.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 41.04 points at 3,338.56 points in pre-bourse electronic dealings. The DAX ended bourse trade on Monday down 60.15 points at 3,279.90 points.

Dealings were expected to focus on the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. consumer price data and its impact on market sentiment as to whether the Federal Reserve would have more scope to raise short-term interest rates at its next meeting in May.

But some traders said the German market was still underpinned by domestic fundamentals, including the weaker mark and relatively low interest rates, and that the DAX should remain between 3,200 and 3,400 points in the near-term.
Carmaker shares were at the forefront, with Volkswagen AG, BMW AG and Daimler all posting gains based on support from the dollar at 1.73 marks.

The gains came despite the European car manufacturers' association ACEA saying on Tuesday that west European car registrations fell three percent year-on-year in March to 1.24 million units, with market leader VW posting no growth.
